title: Easy Rx Cycle Product & Compliance Certification

questions.q: What does Easy Rx Cycle do?
o: Hauls general trash on a route
DEA-registered destruction of pharmaceutical and medical waste through prepaid mail-back kits
Buys back expired drugs for credit
questions.e: We sell prepaid mail-back kits for every regulated pharmaceutical and medical waste stream, then destroy the contents and document it.

questions.q: Which rule prevents most ordering and shipping mistakes?
o: Fill every kit to the top
questions.e: Each kit takes one kind of waste. Mixing streams breaks the destruction rules for both.

questions.q: A customer has used needles and expired non-controlled tablets. What do they need?
o: A Sharps kit and a Pharmaceutical kit
questions.e: Two streams means two kits: sharps go in the Sharps kit, non-controlled drugs go in the Pharmaceutical kit.

questions.q: Which of these does Easy Rx Cycle NOT accept?
questions.e: Pathological waste, formaldehyde, laboratory chemicals and radioactive waste are out of scope.

questions.q: What document proves destruction on every mail-back order?
questions.e: Every returned mail-back kit gets a Certificate of Destruction.

questions.q: Which statement should you NOT make to a customer?
o: You can log in to a portal to see your records
You get a Certificate of Destruction on every mail-back order
questions.e: End customers receive their records by email and mail. Don't promise a customer portal.

questions.q: Can drug waste be flushed or poured down a drain?
o: No. Drug waste should never be sewered
questions.e: EPA bans sewering hazardous waste pharmaceuticals, and controlled substances must be destroyed to a non-retrievable standard with records.

questions.q: A customer has a waste stream you're unsure about. What do you do?
o: Have them ship it and see
Call Easy Rx Cycle at 501-904-2929 before they ship
Tell them to throw it away
questions.e: When in doubt, call before anything ships.

questions.q: A customer asks for Easy Rx Cycle's DEA registration number. What do you say?
o: Read it from the kit label
It's available on request through Easy Rx Cycle
questions.e: We don't publish our DEA number. Customers request it through Easy Rx Cycle.

questions.q: Which item belongs in the Sharps kit?
questions.e: Needles, syringes, lancets, pen needles, auto-injectors and blades go in the Sharps kit.

questions.q: How full can a sharps container be filled?
o: To the fill line, about three-quarters full
questions.e: Stop at the fill line. Overfilled containers are the most common inspection finding.

questions.q: Where do chemo-contaminated needles go?
questions.e: Chemo-contaminated sharps go in the yellow Trace Chemo container, which is incinerated.

questions.q: How are sharps destroyed?
questions.e: Sharps and biohazard waste are autoclave-sterilized.

questions.q: Which federal standard covers handling sharps in the workplace?
questions.e: OSHA's Bloodborne Pathogens Standard governs sharps in the workplace; DOT and state rules cover shipping and treatment.

questions.q: What documents does a Sharps customer receive?
o: Certificate of Destruction and Medical Waste Manifest
questions.e: Sharps and biohazard customers get a Certificate of Destruction and a Medical Waste Manifest.

questions.q: Can a home injector mail back sharps in a milk jug?
o: Only if it is taped shut
No. Sharps must be in the FDA-cleared container
questions.e: Milk jugs, coffee cans and loose bags are never acceptable containers.

questions.q: Which sharps size fits a single home user or a very low-volume office?
questions.e: Sizes run 1 quart to 28 gallon. Pick one they'll fill in weeks to months; the 1 quart suits home users.

questions.q: What's the simple test for whether an item is regulated medical waste?
o: Would it drip or flake blood or other potentially infectious material if squeezed?
questions.e: Items saturated or caked with blood or OPIM are regulated medical waste.

questions.q: A glove with a single dot of dried blood is usually:
questions.e: It wouldn't drip or flake blood, so it's usually regular trash. When unsure, ask.

questions.q: Can loose sharps go in the Biohazard kit?
o: No. Sharps go in the Sharps kit
questions.e: Sharps need a puncture-resistant container. Keep them out of the red bag.

questions.q: Is the red bag alone an acceptable shipping container?
o: No. It must be inside the rigid, UN-rated box
questions.e: The red bag lines the rigid box. The box is the shipping container.

questions.q: Does the Biohazard kit accept pathological waste (tissue)?
questions.e: Pathological waste is out of scope.

questions.q: Who is the main regulator of regulated medical waste?
questions.e: States are the main authority for RMW, alongside OSHA and DOT.

questions.q: How is biohazard waste destroyed?
questions.e: Biohazard waste is autoclave-sterilized.

questions.q: Which of these belongs in the Biohazard kit?
questions.e: Blood-soaked gauze, contaminated PPE, cultures and swabs are biohazard.

questions.q: What goes in the Pharmaceutical kit?
o: Expired non-controlled prescription drugs, OTC drugs and samples
questions.e: Non-controlled, non-hazardous medications, including OTC, samples and vitamins.

questions.q: A clinic has expired hydrocodone. Which kit?
questions.e: Hydrocodone is Schedule II. Controlled substances use the Controlled Substance kit.

questions.q: Expired nicotine gum and warfarin tablets (P-listed) go in:
questions.e: P-listed and U-listed drugs are RCRA hazardous and go in the black RCRA kit.

questions.q: A customer isn't sure whether a drug is hazardous. What should they do?
questions.e: When unsure, treat it as hazardous. Our team can also help classify it.

questions.q: How is pharmaceutical waste destroyed?
questions.e: Pharmaceutical waste is destroyed by regulated incineration.

questions.q: What does the Pharmaceutical kit Certificate of Destruction list?
questions.e: Non-controlled CODs list containers by weight, with a total.

questions.q: What color is the pharmaceutical waste container?
questions.e: Blue = pharmaceutical, red = medical waste, yellow = trace chemo, black = RCRA.

questions.q: An IV bag that held only saline with no hazardous drug goes in:
questions.e: IV bags with no hazardous drug are non-hazardous pharmaceutical waste.

questions.q: The Medication Disposal Mail-Back kit is designed for:
questions.e: It's a tamper-evident mailer for patient and consumer medications.

questions.q: Can a pharmacy put its own expired controlled inventory in the Medication Mail-Back kit?
o: No. A registrant's own controlled inventory uses the Controlled Substance kit
questions.e: The mail-back kit is for patients' medications. A registrant's own controls need the DEA transfer paperwork of the Controlled kit.

questions.q: Can patients' controlled substances go in the Medication Mail-Back kit?
o: Yes, commingled with their other medications
questions.e: Patient take-back allows controlled and non-controlled medications together.

questions.q: Does the On-Site kit come with a Certificate of Destruction?
o: No. Nothing ships back, so no Certificate is issued
questions.e: No return means no Easy Rx Cycle documents. Customers who need a Certificate should use a mail-back kit.

questions.q: Where do full activated-charcoal disposal containers go?
questions.e: The Activated Charcoal Take-Back kit returns them for documented destruction.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT accepted in the Medication Disposal kits?
questions.e: Inhalers, aerosols, sharps, chemo and illicit drugs are not accepted.

questions.q: Who can buy the Controlled Substance kit?
questions.e: Controlled kits are for DEA registrants. We validate the DEA number when the kit comes back.

questions.q: What does the customer fill out for a Controlled kit?
questions.e: One list: company, DEA number, state, and each drug's name, strength, NDC and package size. We do the DEA forms.

questions.q: Schedule II drugs with an NDC are transferred on:
questions.e: Schedule I and II transfers require DEA Form 222.

questions.q: Schedule III, IV and V drugs are transferred on:
questions.e: Schedules III–V use our 3–5 Form.

questions.q: What does DEA Form 41 record?
o: The destruction: what was destroyed, when, how and who witnessed it
questions.e: Form 41 is the Registrant Record of Controlled Substances Destroyed.

questions.q: Who completes the DEA Form 222 and Form 41?
questions.e: We complete them. The customer fills out one list.

questions.q: Controlled substances must be destroyed to which standard?
questions.e: DEA requires destruction to a non-retrievable state.

questions.q: How is controlled-substance destruction priced?
o: By weight (lbs) and the NDCs (drug line items) being destroyed
Per box, no matter what's inside
questions.e: Controlled pricing is based on weight in pounds and the NDCs on the customer's Drug Inventory Manifest. Over 100 lbs is a custom quote.

questions.q: How long should customers keep DEA records?
o: At least 2 years (longer if the state requires)
questions.e: DEA records must be kept at least 2 years.

questions.q: How many witnesses are present for controlled destruction?
questions.e: Two witnesses, who sign by hand.

questions.q: What does "RCRA-empty" mean?
o: All contents removed by normal means; only a trace remains
The container was rinsed with water
questions.e: RCRA-empty containers hold only a trace. That's what the Trace Chemo kit takes.

questions.q: An IV bag with visible chemo drug left in it is:
o: Bulk chemo, not accepted as trace (contact us)
questions.e: Visible drug remaining means it isn't RCRA-empty. That's bulk.

questions.q: What color is the Trace Chemo container?
questions.e: Yellow = trace chemo.

questions.q: Which standard governs handling hazardous drugs like chemo in healthcare?
questions.e: USP <800> covers hazardous drug handling, with OSHA, EPA and DOT.

questions.q: How is trace chemo destroyed?
questions.e: Trace chemo must be incinerated.

questions.q: Chemo-contaminated gowns and gloves go in:
questions.e: Trace-contaminated PPE goes in the yellow Trace Chemo container.

questions.q: Match the color code: black container =
questions.e: Red = medical waste, blue = pharmaceutical, yellow = trace chemo, black = RCRA.

questions.q: Does a customer need a DEA registration to buy the RCRA kit?
o: No. RCRA is EPA, not DEA
questions.e: RCRA is an EPA program. No DEA registration is needed.

questions.q: Nicotine (gum, patches, e-liquid) is:
questions.e: Nicotine is P-listed, so it goes in the RCRA kit.

questions.q: The P and U lists of hazardous wastes are in:
questions.e: EPA's hazardous waste lists are in 40 CFR 261.

questions.q: What does EPA's Subpart P (40 CFR 266) ban?
o: Putting hazardous waste pharmaceuticals down any drain
questions.e: Subpart P is an absolute ban on sewering hazardous waste pharmaceuticals.

questions.q: What color is the RCRA container?
questions.e: Black = RCRA hazardous.

questions.q: What documents does an RCRA customer receive?
o: Certificate of Destruction and Uniform Hazardous Waste Manifest (EPA Form 8700-22)
questions.e: RCRA waste is tracked on the EPA manifest and gets a Certificate of Destruction.

questions.q: Where is RCRA waste destroyed?
o: Incineration at a permitted hazardous-waste facility (TSDF)
questions.e: RCRA waste goes to a permitted treatment, storage and disposal facility (TSDF).

questions.q: EPA waste code D001 means the waste is:
questions.e: D001 = ignitable, D002 = corrosive.

questions.q: What should an RCRA customer have ready if they have one?
questions.e: The EPA ID goes on the hazardous waste manifest.

questions.q: What is the Activated Charcoal Take-Back kit for?
o: Returning used activated-charcoal disposal containers for documented destruction
questions.e: It returns full charcoal disposal containers for destruction with a Certificate.

questions.q: Do the charcoal containers have to be Easy Rx Cycle brand?
questions.e: Any activated-charcoal disposal product is accepted.

questions.q: How is the Charcoal Take-Back kit priced?
o: By weight: up to 5, 25 or 50 lbs
questions.e: Weigh the filled containers and pick the tier.

questions.q: What does the customer fill out for a Charcoal kit?
o: The enclosed disposal manifest listing the containers returned
questions.e: The disposal manifest goes in the box. They receive a Certificate of Destruction and a copy of their manifest.

questions.q: A customer has 70 lbs of charcoal containers. What do you do?
o: Order multiple kits or ask Easy Rx Cycle for a freight quote
questions.e: Over 50 lbs: multiple kits or a freight quote.

questions.q: Can loose medications go in the Charcoal Take-Back kit?
o: No. Use the right mail-back kit
questions.e: The kit is for used charcoal containers only.

questions.q: Which form does federal law require for every transfer of Schedule I and II drugs?
questions.e: Schedule I and II transfers require the official DEA Form 222.

questions.q: Who issues the official DEA Form 222?
questions.e: Official 222s are issued by DEA. We print the transfer data onto the official form.

questions.q: On the 222 for a returned kit, the customer is listed as the:
questions.e: The customer supplies the drugs to Easy Rx Cycle, so they're the supplier.

questions.q: What does each line of a 222 include?
o: Number of packages, package size, name of item and NDC
questions.e: Every line carries packages, package size, item name and the NDC, plus shipped and received counts and dates.

questions.q: A customer's kit holds 25 Schedule II line items. How many 222s are needed?
o: Two — each form holds up to 20 lines
questions.e: Each 222 holds up to 20 lines, so 25 lines need two forms.

questions.q: Which schedules go on the 3–5 Form?
questions.e: The 3–5 Form documents Schedule III, IV and V transfers.

questions.q: A Schedule II item has no NDC. Which transfer form is it recorded on?
questions.e: Schedule I/II items without an NDC are recorded on the 3–5 Form.

questions.q: Whose name appears as the purchaser on the 3–5 Form?
questions.e: Arkansas Redistributors, LLC is Easy Rx Cycle's legal name. The customer is the supplier.

questions.q: What does "last line completed" on the 3–5 Form record?
o: The number of the last line used — 20 or less
questions.e: It closes the form so no lines can be added. More than 20 items means another form.

questions.q: Who completes the 222 and the 3–5 Form for a kit return?
o: Easy Rx Cycle, from the customer's Drug Inventory Manifest
questions.e: The customer fills out one list; we prepare the transfer forms from it.

questions.q: Who completes DEA Form 41?
o: Easy Rx Cycle, as the destroying registrant
questions.e: We destroy the drugs, so we complete and keep Form 41.

questions.q: Which details are recorded on DEA Form 41?
o: NDC, substance, strength, form, quantity destroyed, plus the date, method and location of destruction
questions.e: Form 41 documents exactly what was destroyed and how, when and where.

questions.q: How is DEA Form 41 signed?
questions.e: Two witnesses sign Form 41 by hand.

questions.q: Which forms come with a Controlled kit that contained Schedule II and Schedule IV drugs?
o: DEA Form 222, the 3–5 Form, DEA Form 41 and the Certificate of Destruction
questions.e: Schedule II on the 222, Schedule IV on the 3–5 Form, the destruction on Form 41, plus the Certificate.

modules.title: Certificates of Destruction, manifests & EPA forms

questions.q: Which document comes with every mail-back product?
questions.e: Every returned mail-back kit gets a Certificate of Destruction.

questions.q: A Sharps Certificate of Destruction lists:
o: Containers and weights, with autoclave as the method
questions.e: Non-controlled CODs list containers by weight and the stream's destruction method.

questions.q: A controlled-substance Certificate of Destruction lists:
o: Each drug's name, strength, NDC, form and quantity, plus the client DEA number and witnesses
questions.e: Controlled CODs itemize every drug and are signed by hand.

questions.q: How are non-controlled Certificates of Destruction signed?
o: Electronically, by the operator and the CEO
questions.e: Non-controlled CODs carry two electronic signatures. Controlled CODs are signed by hand.

questions.q: What is the Certificate of Destruction's main job for the customer?
o: Proof of destruction they can show an inspector
questions.e: The COD is the customer's proof the material was destroyed — how and when.

questions.q: Every Certificate of Destruction carries:
o: A certificate number and issue date
questions.e: Each COD has a unique certificate number and issue date.

questions.q: Which destruction method prints on an RCRA Certificate of Destruction?
questions.e: RCRA waste goes to a permitted treatment, storage and disposal facility.

questions.q: Which Certificate of Destruction shows the client's DEA number and the two witnesses?
questions.e: Only the controlled COD carries the DEA number and witnesses.

questions.q: Which products come with a Medical Waste Manifest?
questions.e: The Medical Waste Manifest tracks regulated medical waste: sharps, biohazard and trace chemo.

questions.q: What does the Medication Disposal On-Site kit come with from Easy Rx Cycle?
questions.e: On-site deactivation happens at the customer's location, so we issue nothing.

questions.q: What does the Medical Waste Manifest record about the waste?
o: Number of containers, total weight and treatment method
questions.e: It tracks containers, weight and treatment, with signatures at each step.

questions.q: On the Medical Waste Manifest, the "generator" is:
o: The customer who produced the waste
questions.e: The generator is the facility that produced the waste — the customer.

questions.q: EPA Form 8700-22 tracks hazardous waste:
o: Cradle to grave: generator, transporter, treatment facility
questions.e: The Uniform Hazardous Waste Manifest follows RCRA waste from generator to TSDF.

questions.q: EPA waste codes such as P075 and U058 appear on which form?
questions.e: Hazardous waste codes go on the Uniform Hazardous Waste Manifest.

questions.q: Which ID should an RCRA customer provide for the EPA manifest?
questions.e: The generator's EPA ID goes on the RCRA Form.

questions.q: What does the TSDF on the EPA manifest stand for?
questions.e: The TSDF is the permitted facility that receives and treats the hazardous waste.

questions.q: The U.S. DOT description on the EPA manifest includes:
o: Proper shipping name, hazard class, UN number and packing group
questions.e: DOT shipping details describe the hazardous material for transport.

questions.q: How long should customers keep EPA hazardous waste manifests?
questions.e: Keep hazardous waste manifests at least 3 years, longer if the state requires.

questions.q: An Activated Charcoal Take-Back customer receives:
o: A Certificate of Destruction and a copy of their disposal manifest
questions.e: They get a COD plus a copy of the disposal manifest they enclosed.

questions.q: Where does a distributor place bulk orders?
o: In the Easy Rx Cycle partner portal (Place an Order)
questions.e: Distributors order in the partner portal.

questions.q: Where are distributor bulk orders shipped?
questions.e: Kits ship in bulk to your warehouse. You resell from your stock.

questions.q: Does the waste ever pass through the distributor?
o: No. The customer mails the full kit directly to Easy Rx Cycle
questions.e: You sell an empty kit. The waste goes straight from your customer to us.

questions.q: What does every kit include for the return trip?
questions.e: Every kit includes its prepaid return label.

questions.q: When should you bring Easy Rx Cycle into a deal?
o: Pickups, multiple sites, volume above the largest kit, or law-enforcement destruction
questions.e: Those need a custom quote.

questions.q: A customer says, "We already use a big hauler." Best answer?
o: "Keep them for what they do well. Mail-back fills the gaps with no contract."
questions.e: Mail-back covers controlled substances, small volumes and extra locations.

questions.q: A customer says, "We just flush it." Best answer?
o: "Drug waste can't go down the drain, and controlled substances must be destroyed to DEA's non-retrievable standard with records."
questions.e: Flushing is never compliant.

questions.q: Which price is shown in this playbook?
questions.e: The playbook shows MSRP only.

questions.q: A customer wants a Controlled kit but isn't DEA-registered and collects patients' medications. What do you sell?
questions.e: Non-registrants collecting patients' medications use the Medication Disposal kits.
